passages.text: And, so that I do not prolong for you words that are unnecessary, I lived with her because of her devotion to her husband. Before long, my hands—wretched woman that I am—were paralyzed by attacks of biting pain, and the woman who had taken me in, her whole body bound by some affliction, lies prostrate at home. Since, then, the compassion of the women from before has waned, and both I and the woman at home are incapacitated, for many years I have sat here, as you see, begging; and whatever I manage to obtain, I also carry home for my fellow sufferer’s sustenance. So much for my own affairs; let them have been told sufficiently. What remains is that you are preventing the fulfillment of your promise to give me the drug, so that I may give it to her as well, since she desires to die, and in this way I too may be able to depart from life, as you said.”

lexical_decisions.chosen: because of her devotion to her husband
lexical_decisions.rationale: φιλανδρία denotes love of or devotion to a husband. The immediate context favors the poor widow’s devotion, though the phrase could encompass the narrator’s corresponding marital devotion.

lexical_decisions.chosen: were paralyzed by attacks of biting pain
lexical_decisions.rationale: δήγματα literally denotes bites or stings and can describe sharp, biting pains; a more literal alternative is “were disabled by the bites.”

lexical_decisions.chosen: her whole body bound by some affliction
lexical_decisions.rationale: ὅλη indicates that the affliction affected her wholly, while συνδεθεῖσα retains the image of being bound.
The perfect ἔρριπται presents the resulting prostrate condition as continuing at the time of the woman’s account; “has been laid prostrate at home” is another possible rendering.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἐγὼ δὲ καὶ ἡ κατ’ οἶκον ἀμφότεραι ἐπισινεῖς τυγχάνομεν
lexical_decisions.chosen: both I and the woman at home are incapacitated
lexical_decisions.rationale: The present τυγχάνομεν describes both women as currently harmed, impaired, or afflicted, explaining their continuing need.
εὐπορέω here concerns securing available resources rather than being generally wealthy.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: καὶ τῇ συνταλαιπώρῳ εἰς τροφὰς κομίζω
lexical_decisions.chosen: I also carry home for my fellow sufferer’s sustenance
lexical_decisions.rationale: εἰς τροφὰς expresses the purpose of what she brings—providing nourishment or sustenance—without requiring that everything obtained be edible.
φάρμακον can mean medicine, drug, or poison. “Drug” preserves the lexical breadth, while the expressed desire for death supplies the lethal purpose in context.
The construction is a euphemism for dying, literally involving a change or departure from living.
